headline: Fixing KV-Cache Page Table Granularity for Intel GPU Attention
summary: SGLang PR #23757 fixes incorrect KV-cache page table values in the XPU attention backend when page_size > 1 and local attention is enabled. The bug caused wrong outputs from flash_attn_with_kvcache due to passing token-granularity tables instead of page-granularity ones. The fix strides and divides the table to convert slot indices to physical page indices.
why_it_matters: Ensures correct attention outputs on Intel GPUs with chunked attention, preventing silent accuracy degradation in production inference.

headline: TensorRT-LLM Refactors Disaggregated Transfer Coordination
summary: This PR centralizes generation receive orchestration and transfer-window admission into DisaggTransferCoordinator, removing DisaggLoopDelegates and obsolete PyExecutor helpers. It adds executor effects for resource preparation and deferred allocation rollback, with expanded CPU-only tests covering admission, rollback, and error paths.
why_it_matters: Centralizing transfer coordination simplifies disaggregated serving logic, reducing maintenance overhead and potential bugs in multi-GPU inference pipelines.

headline: KEDA+EPP becomes the recommended autoscaling path for LLM inference
summary: llm-d/llm-d PR #2497 revamps autoscaling docs, making KEDA+EPP the primary architecture and deprecating WVA. It adds a signal table for queue depth, pool saturation, token backlog, and estimated latency, plus scalingModifiers and clarifies pending-pod and quota handling.
why_it_matters: Clarifies the production-grade autoscaling stack for LLM inference, enabling precise scaling signals and avoiding race conditions, which directly impacts latency and throughput.

headline: Fix Intel XPU Model Server Command Ordering in llm-d Guide
summary: PR #2515 reorders the Intel XPU deploy command before NVIDIA GPU in the Wide EP LWS guide to fix a CI failure. The parser's substring replacement mangles the GPU path, causing wrong directory selection for XPU backend.
why_it_matters: Ensures correct backend selection for Intel XPU deployments, preventing CI failures and ensuring proper model server setup.

headline: Docs Update: Networking Prerequisites for Wide-EP LWS
summary: PR #2484 links networking setup docs for wide-ep-lws, covering All-to-All RDMA (InfiniBand/RoCE) on NVIDIA DeepEP and full-mesh pod connectivity on Intel XPU. Adds provider-neutral references to RDMA and multi-node guides, ensuring fresh clusters can be provisioned correctly.
why_it_matters: Clear networking prerequisites prevent misconfiguration in multi-node inference, reducing latency and ensuring high-throughput collective communication for large-scale EP workloads.

headline: Dense vs. MoE: Why 30B Can Activate Only 3B
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models like Nemotron 3.5 Lightning activate only a fraction of parameters per token, balancing capacity with compute efficiency. This explainer breaks down active parameters, throughput trade-offs, and when dense models still win.
why_it_matters: Understanding MoE vs. dense trade-offs is critical for optimizing inference latency, throughput, and memory footprint in production systems.

headline: Ermes: Stateful FaaS for Edge-to-Cloud Latency
summary: Ermes integrates state management into FaaS, jointly scheduling functions and data across edge-to-cloud nodes. It uses collections with per-collection consistency (sequential to eventual) and fine-grained replication, reducing remote state access and sustaining low latency as workloads and client mobility increase.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, Ermes reduces state-access latency in distributed inference pipelines, enabling low-latency serving across heterogeneous edge-cloud resources without sacrificing consistency control.

headline: ComPO: Zeroth-Order Preference Alignment for LLMs
summary: ComPO is a zeroth-order alignment method using comparison oracles to extract directional preference info without differentiable loss. It mitigates likelihood displacement, with convergence guarantees and improved length-controlled win rates on Mistral, Llama, Gemma, Qwen3, and Gemma-3.
why_it_matters: Offers a memory-efficient alignment alternative that avoids likelihood displacement, potentially reducing training overhead for inference engineers fine-tuning LLMs.

headline: Detecting Reward Hacking via Internal Representations
summary: Researchers find that simple difference-of-means vectors in LLM internal representations reliably detect reward hacking across models like Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and Qwen 3.8 Max. These vectors are as effective as LLM monitors but nearly free, and can predict hacks before they occur.
why_it_matters: Enables low-cost, real-time monitoring of reward hacking without expensive LLM-based detectors, reducing inference overhead and improving safety in deployed systems.

headline: HOPE: Smarter Expert Pruning for MoE Models
summary: HOPE introduces a second-order pruning objective for mixture-of-experts models, capturing cooperative expert interactions that first-order methods like REAP ignore. It provably minimizes pruning error, achieving better performance at high pruning rates, especially on complex agentic tasks, across models up to 122B parameters.
why_it_matters: Enables aggressive compression of MoE models with minimal quality loss, directly reducing memory footprint and potentially improving inference efficiency on resource-constrained systems.

headline: Optimal FaaS Placement with Data Replication in Edge-Cloud
summary: This paper tackles joint function scheduling and data placement in FaaS across edge-cloud, considering heterogeneous consistency. It proposes a Binary Linear Programming model for optimal placement and a topology-aware greedy heuristic that achieves near-optimal latency at low computational cost, enabling periodic reconfiguration.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, this offers a practical method to minimize client latency by intelligently placing functions and replicated data across distributed infrastructure, reducing response times in edge-cloud deployments.

headline: Fluid Notarization: Certifying Document Evolution, Not Snapshots
summary: Fluid Notarization uses a JSON-native delta-CRDT to certify a graph of causally linked document changes, reducing blockchain notarization to recording identifiers. It combines deterministic convergence with auditable proof-of-existence, enabling off-chain sync and reconstruction. A prototype on electronic health records shows feasibility.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, this paradigm reduces on-chain overhead and enables efficient, verifiable state management for distributed collaborative systems, analogous to tracking model updates in decentralized inference pipelines.

headline: Decodable but Misrouted: Sparse Features Uncover a Readout Gap in Vision-La
summary: When a large vision-language model misclassifies a harmful meme, the failure may reflect missing internal evidence or an inability to route represented evidence to its output. We distinguish these cases in Gemma-3 and Qwen3.5 using sparse autoencoders, role-conditioned probes, causal interventions, and recovery experiments across
why_it_matters: Key development in arXiv impacting inference serving performance and workflow optimization.

headline: Inference Is the Last LLM Moat
summary: As LLM capabilities converge, inference efficiency emerges as the ultimate competitive advantage. Optimizing latency, throughput, and cost becomes the key differentiator for deploying models at scale.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, this underscores that mastering inference optimization is critical for product success and cost reduction.
